subject: Private deployment — Day 0 access, routing, and control-plane checklist
messages:
From: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@falkon.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-eng@falkon.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Falkon day-0 — firewall, routing, and access questions

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the quick onboarding sync last week. We're planning Day 0 (network activation + control-plane handoff) for 31 Dec and wanted to confirm the minimum items you need from our side so there's no surprise on cutover. High level ask: what exact IPs/subnets you need on our firewall, any NAT/egress constraints, service account names, and PKI/KMS owner details.

Attached is our current perimeter allowlist export (falkon-fw-allowlist-v1.csv). A few specifics:
- We're running a pair of NAT gateways in us-west-2 with outgoing SNAT.
- Preferred bastion IP will be 54.243.88.12 (subject to change based on ASN).
- We have a corporate KMS in AWS (alias/keys/falkon-prod).

Also looping in infra-eng for the routing and procurement mailbox for any contract/comms. If you can send a Day 0 checklist I can tick items off on our side and return confirmations.

Best,
Thomas Reed
Head of Infrastructure
Falkon AI

Attachment: falkon-fw-allowlist-v1.csv (CSV - 24 KB)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@falkon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Falkon day-0 — firewall, routing, and access questions

Thomas — thanks for the export, that helps. Below is the condensed Day 0 checklist we expect for a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment. I've called out items that require confirmation from your infra team.

Required before handoff (please confirm):
1) IP allowlist: outbound IP ranges we will use for control-plane callbacks: 34.203.11.0/24, 34.203.12.0/24 (please confirm these can be added to your egress allowlist).
2) Bastion: a static public IP and SSH user account (we prefer named svc-redwood-bastion for audit).
3) KMS/GCP/Azure key alias: user must provide key ARN/Resource ID and a service account principal for encryption-decrypt roles.
4) Peering/Transit: VPC peering or private link (we support both) — confirm whether you prefer AWS VPC peering or a Transit Gateway route table approach.
5) Service accounts & IAM: list of service account emails we should grant the control-plane principal to (minimum: cloud-readonly, kms-encrypt, network-admin).
6) DNS delegation: the hostnames we should register and whether you want Route53 delegated or CNAME-based entries.
7) Egress: confirmed NAT IPs for token-revocation callbacks and telemetry.

Optional but recommended for Day 0:
- SSH bastion jumpbox configuration and temporary access window for initial validation.
- A short list of test vectors and sample traffic (1k tokens/s sample) so we can run a smoke validation.

I attached a concise Day 0 workbook (redwood-day0-checklist.xlsx) and will follow up with a technical handoff from Ben for the routing/nat specifics. If anything needs to be elevated to procurement/contracting (SLA/ingress terms), Kimberly is cc'd.

Thanks — I'll hold a stub slot on 31 Dec 09:00 PT for the handoff unless you need a different time.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-day0-checklist.xlsx (XLSX - 12 KB)
From: Falkon AI Infrastructure <infra-eng@falkon.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@falkon.ai>, procurement@falkon.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Falkon day-0 — firewall, routing, and access questions

Lukas/Ben — quick answers from infra team:
- We can add the two /24 blocks you listed to the egress allowlist; we'll add them to the perimeter on Thu 31 Dec 02:00 PT (maintenance window).
- Bastion IP: 54.243.88.12 is confirmed for initial test; we'll provide key material for svc-redwood-bastion via secure transfer.
- KMS: AWS key alias arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:alias/falkon-prod — we can add the Redwood control-plane principal (principal id to be provided).
- Peering: we prefer Transit Gateway attachment for future scaling; we'll open the TGW route table to the VPC you supply.
- Service accounts: infra will create a service account redwood-integration@falkon.ai with the least privilege roles (cloud-readonly, kms-use, network-op).

Attached is a sanitized copy of the firewall CSV with comments and our bastion handoff notes (bastion-handoff-notes.pdf).

Two asks for Redwood to confirm:
A) Which hostname scheme will you register for control-plane callbacks (control.redwood.<customer-domain> vs callbacks.<customer-domain>)? We need this for TLS cert procurement.
B) Can you confirm length of the temporary validation window (we typically allow 2 business days for smoke tests).

Thanks,
Falkon AI Infra team

Attachments: bastion-handoff-notes.pdf (PDF - 48 KB); falkon-fw-allowlist-v1.csv (CSV - 24 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@falkon.ai>, Falkon AI Infrastructure <infra-eng@falkon.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Falkon day-0 — firewall, routing, and access questions

Thanks for the details — pairing with infra is perfect. A few technical clarifications so our Day 0 runs cleanly:
- Confirm TGW route targets: we will consume a /28 from your VPC for control-plane egress NAT and announce two host routes back to your TGW route table. Please confirm the allocated /28 (we can accept either public or private range, depending on your preference).
- SSH access: we'll request temporary key rotation for svc-redwood-bastion after Day 0 validation. Please provide the initial key via the secure transfer link in the workbook.
- TLS certs: control-plane prefers a SAN list including control.redwood.falkon.ai and telemetry.redwood.falkon.ai — if you prefer callbacks.<domain> that's fine; we just need one canonical scheme.
- Smoke tests: propose 30 minutes of 1k tokens/sec sustained, then a stability ramp to 5k tokens/sec for 15 minutes. Log and latency capture will be shared to your infra S3 bucket (we'll only write diagnostic artifacts to a pre-agreed path).

I'll load a brief runbook into the shared Drive folder and will push a single-run verification playbook so your team can follow it during the maintenance window.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Deployment Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-day0-runbook.md (reference in Drive)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@falkon.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@falkon.ai
Date: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Falkon day-0 — firewall, routing, and access questions

Thomas — confirming procurement and legal have the DocuSign template link; procurement will countersign after the technical checklist is complete. Lukas/Ben — we have a standing SLA exception that requires explicit written acceptance for any maintenance window outside Mon-Fri; Falkon's 31 Dec window is approved for this onboarding only.

As soon as you confirm the hostname scheme and the /28 allocation for control-plane NAT, procurement will finalize the order and issue the onboarding invoice.

Thanks everyone,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
